new.title: Visit Kutlubey Ulu Cami in the old bazaar
new.desc: Kutlubey Ulu Camii is the main congregational mosque of Isparta, set inside the old market quarter. The original mosque is thought to date to 1429, while the present building is from 1922.
new.tip: Combine it with the covered bazaar next door; dress modestly and avoid prayer times.
new.q: Kutlubey Ulu Camii, Kutlubey, Isparta Merkez, Isparta

new.title: Browse Firdevs Bey Bedesteni, the 1561 covered market
new.desc: The Firdevs Bey Bedesteni is a covered bazaar built in 1561 as an income source for the Mimar Sinan (Firdevs Paşa) Mosque. It is built of the local kövke stone, and small shops inside sell souvenirs and local goods.
new.tip: Look for rose products and Isparta rugs; shops are quiet on Sunday.
new.q: Firdevs Bey Bedesteni, Kutlubey, Isparta Merkez, Isparta

new.title: See the Mimar Sinan (Firdevs Paşa) Mosque of 1561
new.desc: This mosque is dated to 1561 and carries the name of the great architect Mimar Sinan, who is credited in local tradition and guides with the work. The Firdevs Bey Bedesteni next to it was built to fund its upkeep.
new.tip: Visit together with the bedesten; the interior is open outside prayer times.
new.q: Mimar Sinan Camii, Kutlubey, Isparta Merkez, Isparta

new.title: See 3,500 rugs at the Turan Yazgan Carpet and Kilim Museum
new.desc: Opened in 2013 by Isparta Municipality at the entrance of the Gökçay recreation area, this museum is billed as the largest carpet and rug museum in Türkiye, with more than 3,500 mostly hand-woven pieces. A large rose sculpture marks the building, and it counted about 110,000 visitors in 2024.
new.tip: Open daily during working hours; allow 1-2 hours and pair it with a walk in Gökçay.
new.q: Halı ve Kilim Müzesi, Gökçay Mesireliği, Emre Mahallesi, Isparta Merkez, Isparta

new.title: Trace perfume history at the Misparta Scent Museum
new.desc: The Misparta Koku Medeniyeti Müzesi occupies the restored Aya Baniya Church, which dates to the 1750s. It presents the history of scent, including a 4,500-year-old perfume formula, and links it to Isparta's rose-oil tradition.
new.tip: Check opening hours with Isparta Municipality before going, as the museum is recent.
new.q: Aya Baniya Kilisesi, Keçeci Mahallesi, Isparta Merkez, Isparta

new.title: Explore the Isparta Museum on Millet Caddesi
new.desc: Isparta Museum, founded in 1985, shows archaeological and ethnographic collections from the province, including copper objects and Yalvaç weavings. It is the best place to put the region's ancient cities in context.
new.tip: Pair it with a visit to Sagalassos or Antioch of Pisidia for the context.
new.q: Isparta Müzesi, Millet Caddesi, Isparta Merkez, Isparta

new.title: Walk the rim of Gölcük crater lake
new.desc: Gölcük is a volcanic maar lake at about 1,380 m, roughly 8 km southwest of Isparta, with rims 150-300 m above the water. It was made a nature park in 1991, and Isparta Municipality took over its operation in 2024.
new.tip: Cooler than the city in summer and good for picnics; take the paved road from town.
new.q: Gölcük Tabiat Parkı, Isparta Merkez, Isparta

new.title: Ski or hike at Davraz Mountain above Eğirdir
new.desc: Davraz (2,635 m) rises between Lake Eğirdir and Lake Kovada, and the ski resort sits about 25 km from both Isparta and Eğirdir. The season runs roughly mid-December to March, and a day section of the St Paul Trail runs from here toward Kasnak Forest.
new.tip: Go on weekdays in winter for shorter queues; in summer the road gives walking and views over the lakes.
new.q: Davraz Kayak Merkezi, Isparta Merkez, Isparta

new.title: Eat lamb şiş at Kebapçı Kadir on Hükümet Meydanı
new.desc: Kebapçı Kadir in the Kebapçılar Arastası by Hükümet Meydanı is one of the best-known grills in central Isparta. It is praised for lamb şiş, Adana kebap and a wide meze selection.
new.tip: Order the lamb şiş with meze; central and busy at lunch.
new.q: Kebapçı Kadir, Kebapçılar Arastası, Hükümet Meydanı, Kutlubey, Isparta Merkez, Isparta

new.title: Try tandır kebabı and kabune pilavı at Hacıbenlioğlu
new.desc: Hacıbenlioğlu Kebap Helva ve Pide Salonu is an old-established Isparta restaurant that traces its service to 1833. It is recommended for tandır kebabı and is a listed place for kabune pilavı, the rice cooked in copper pots that is Isparta's festive dish.
new.tip: Ask for kabune pilavı with the white bean and meat stew, and finish with the house helva.
new.q: Hacıbenlioğlu Kebap Helva ve Pide Salonu, Isparta Merkez, Isparta

new.title: Tour the 1950s Gülbirlik rose-oil factory in Güneykent
new.desc: The Güneykent rose-oil plant dates to the 1950s and was folded into the Gülbirlik cooperative in 1977. Visitors see its old stills and a steam engine, and a small rose museum called Güze shows 150-year-old distilling equipment.
new.tip: Best in the May-June season when the distilleries run; ask Gülbirlik or the Güneykent municipality about visiting hours.
new.q: Güneykent Gülyağı Fabrikası, Güneykent, Gönen, Isparta

new.title: Walk the Eğirdir castle on its lake causeway
new.desc: Eğirdir Castle stands on a narrow spit reaching into the lake and guarded the town from the water side. Its present form is Roman or Byzantine, with an inscription of 1307 recording a restoration by Dündar Bey.
new.tip: Free to walk; the lake views are best at sunset.
new.q: Eğirdir Kalesi, Eğirdir, Isparta

new.title: Browse the stone Dündar Bey Medresesi in Eğirdir
new.desc: This Seljuk and Hamidid building began as an inn in 1237 and became a madrasa under Dündar Bey around 1301. It was restored in the 1960s and now houses a small bazaar of crafts.
new.tip: Quiet in the morning; combine it with the Hızır Bey mosque across the street.
new.q: Dündar Bey Medresesi, Eğirdir, Isparta

new.title: Step into Hızır Bey (Ulu) Cami opposite the madrasa
new.desc: Hızır Bey Camii, locally called the Ulu Cami, stands directly opposite the Dündar Bey Medresesi. It is the main mosque of Eğirdir's old town and is used by locals daily.
new.tip: Visit outside prayer times and dress modestly.
new.q: Hızır Bey Camii, Eğirdir, Isparta

new.title: Cross the causeway to Yeşilada island
new.desc: Yeşilada is a small island joined to Eğirdir by a causeway, home to a Greek community until 1923. Stone-based wooden houses, narrow lanes and fishermen's shelters fill its nine hectares.
new.tip: Go in the evening when the lake turns pink; the island has pensions and fish restaurants.
new.q: Yeşilada, Eğirdir, Isparta

new.title: Eat lake fish at Felekabad on Yeşilada
new.desc: Felekabad is a restaurant on the end of Yeşilada island, with views over Lake Eğirdir. Reviews mention the atmosphere and the limited menu of lake fish.
new.tip: Ask what was caught that day; crayfish season is closed from mid-November, so check before you go.
new.q: Felekabad Restaurant, Yeşilada, Eğirdir, Isparta

new.title: Hike and paddle at Kovada Lake National Park
new.desc: Kovada Lake National Park lies about 29 km south of Eğirdir, fed by a canal from Lake Eğirdir. Forest, marked walking paths and bird-watching make it a quiet nature day.
new.tip: Visit in spring or autumn; bring water as services are limited.
new.q: Kovada Gölü Milli Parkı, Eğirdir, Isparta

new.title: Walk through the 765 m Zindan Cave in Aksu
new.desc: Zindan Cave lies about 2 km northeast of Aksu, at around 1,300 m, and is lit along 765 m of passages. It is entered across a Roman bridge and has stalactites, stalagmites and a calcite-crystal hamam chamber at the end.
new.tip: The cave stays cool all year, so bring a jacket.
new.q: Zindan Mağarası, Aksu, Isparta

new.title: Hike Yazılı Canyon Nature Park near Sütçüler
new.desc: Yazılı Canyon is a 546-hectare nature park, declared in 1989, about 80 km south of Isparta. It is named after an ancient inscription cut into a rock in the canyon, and it has walking and climbing routes.
new.tip: Go early; the park is day-use only with no lodging.
new.q: Yazılı Kanyon Tabiat Parkı, Çandır, Sütçüler, Isparta

new.title: Find the Pisidian ruins at Adada near Sütçüler
new.desc: Adada was a Pisidian city in the mountains of Sütçüler, first identified in 1888 by Hirschfeld and Ramsay. Its foundation date is unknown, and many church and chapel remains stand in the hills around it.
new.tip: Reach it by car; wear sturdy shoes as the ruins are open and uneven.
new.q: Adada Antik Kenti, Sütçüler, Isparta

new.title: Stand where St Paul preached at Antioch of Pisidia
new.desc: Antioch of Pisidia, near modern Yalvaç, has a theatre, aqueducts and a rock-cut Temple of Augustus. The great basilica, linked by excavators with the Church of St Paul, is tied to Paul's first recorded sermon (Acts 13).
new.tip: Allow 2-3 hours; it is exposed, so go in spring or autumn and visit the Yalvaç Museum afterwards.
new.q: Pisidia Antiokheia Antik Kenti, Yalvaç, Isparta

new.title: See the finds of Antioch at Yalvaç Museum
new.desc: Yalvaç Museum displays the finds from Antioch of Pisidia and the surrounding area. It opens seven days a week from 08:00 to 16:30 according to the ministry listing.
new.tip: Go after the ruins; confirm hours locally as they change.
new.q: Yalvaç Müzesi, Yalvaç, Isparta

new.title: Climb to Uluborlu Castle over the town
new.desc: Uluborlu Castle crowns the town of Uluborlu, between Isparta and Dinar. It is known for its view from the walls, and the town also has a museum and a Seljuk bath.
new.tip: Pair it with a bowl of Uluborlu banak, the district's GI-registered lamb-and-pide dish.
new.q: Uluborlu Kalesi, Uluborlu, Isparta

new.title: Sail or canoe on Karacaören Dam Lake
new.desc: Karacaören-1 is a 93 m earth-fill dam on the Aksu River, completed in 1990, with a reservoir of about 45 km2. The lake is used for sailing, canoeing and shoreside walks.
new.tip: Bring a car; services at the dam are limited.
new.q: Karacaören Barajı, Burdur

new.title: Swim at Lake Salda, the Maldives of Türkiye
new.desc: Salda is a volcanic crater lake in Yeşilova, 196 m deep, with white mineral shores that earned it the nickname Maldives of Türkiye. Visitor numbers are capped, and swimming on the white sand of Beyaz Adalar was banned in 2020, with Halk Plajı and the nature park beaches still open.
new.tip: Go on a weekday in summer and expect limits on visitor numbers.
new.q: Salda Gölü, Yeşilova, Burdur

new.title: Watch the sunset over Lake Burdur from Serenler Hill
new.desc: Serenler Hill Nature Park is about 4 km from central Burdur and has views over Lake Burdur, with picnic areas and walks. Lake Burdur is a Ramsar wetland important for wintering birds.
new.tip: Take a taxi or car; go in the late afternoon for the sunset.
new.q: Serenler Tepesi Tabiat Parkı, Burdur Merkez, Burdur

new.title: See Sagalassos statues at Burdur Archaeological Museum
new.desc: The museum opened in 1969 in the former library of the Bulguroğlu (Pirkulzade) Madrasa and holds tens of thousands of objects. Highlights include a Dionysos statue from Sagalassos and the Dancing Girls frieze, and it won a European Museum Forum award in 2008.
new.tip: Visit before going to Sagalassos or Kibyra to see what was found there.
new.q: Burdur Müzesi, Halk Pazarı Caddesi, Özgür, Burdur Merkez, Burdur

new.title: Visit Burdur Ulu Cami and the 1936 clock tower
new.desc: The Burdur Grand Mosque is a Seljuk-era mosque dating to about 1300, on a high hill, with a restored marble mihrab and pulpit. The 1936 cut-stone clock tower with four clocks stands nearby.
new.tip: Visit outside prayer times.
new.q: Burdur Ulu Camii, Pazar, Burdur Merkez, Burdur

new.title: Admire the başoda of Bakibey Konağı in Burdur
new.desc: Bakibey Mansion is a 17th-century house in central Burdur noted for its main salon (başoda). It is one of the few remaining examples of old Burdur domestic architecture.
new.tip: Check opening times at the Burdur culture and tourism office.
new.q: Bakibey Konağı, Divan Baba Caddesi, Değirmenler Mahallesi, Merkez, Burdur

new.title: Descend into İnsuyu Cave, Türkiye's first show cave
new.desc: İnsuyu Cave, found in 1952 and opened to the public in 1966, was Türkiye's first show cave. It has stalactites, stalagmites and lakes, with a steady 14 C temperature.
new.tip: Bring a jacket; check the current hours and guided-visit rules.
new.q: İnsuyu Mağarası, Burdur Merkez, Burdur

new.title: Explore Sagalassos and its Antonine Fountain at Ağlasun
new.desc: Sagalassos is a Roman-era hilltop city above Ağlasun, known for the restored Antonine Nymphaeum fountain, baths and a theatre that held about 9,000. The fountain was rebuilt from its original pieces between 1998 and 2010.
new.tip: Wear good shoes for the climb and allow half a day; check hours before going.
new.q: Sagalassos Antik Kenti, Ağlasun, Burdur

new.title: See the Medusa mosaic in Kibyra's Odeon at Gölhisar
new.desc: Kibyra has a stadium for about 10,000 and a large Odeon with a Medusa mosaic in opus sectile. The mosaic is covered in winter and reopened for the season, and the site draws roughly 34-40 thousand visitors a year.
new.tip: Visit in the open season (spring to late autumn); it is about 110 km from Burdur.
new.q: Kibyra Antik Kenti, Gölhisar, Burdur

new.title: Climb to Kremna, the Pisidian city above the Aksu valley
new.desc: Kremna in Bucak is a Pisidian and Roman city on a hill above the Aksu valley. Its sculptures are now in the Burdur museum.
new.tip: Reach it by car and expect an open, hilly site.
new.q: Kremna Antik Kenti, Çamlık, Bucak, Burdur

new.title: Eat Burdur şiş at Şişçi Kadir Okan Özen (1985)
new.desc: Burdur şiş is a geographically indicated şiş köfte made from hand-minced goat or beef ribs with salt only, served on thin bread with grilled green pepper. Şişçi Kadir Okan Özen, open since 1985, has more than 4,000 Google reviews and an outdoor seating area.
new.tip: Order a portion of şiş with grilled peppers and ayran; lunch gets busy.
new.q: Burdur Şişçi Kadir Okan Özen 1985, Cümbüşlü Caddesi, Özgür Mahallesi, Merkez, Burdur

new.title: Order sac kavurma at Toros Lokantası in Burdur
new.desc: Toros Lokantası in Burdur Merkez is a very heavily reviewed local lokanta known for sac kavurma and pide. It is a casual, family-friendly place.
new.tip: Share a sac kavurma with bread and salad.
new.q: Toros Lokantası, Oğuz Sokak, Burdur Merkez, Burdur

new.title: Taste Burdur cheese pide at Altay Pide
new.desc: Altay Pide on Hükümet Caddesi is a budget-friendly spot for the local pide with kelle cheese, plus lahmacun and kebabs. Burdur's cheese and minced meat pide is one of the city's signature dishes.
new.tip: Ask for the cheese pide; cheap and quick.
new.q: Altay Pide, Hükümet Caddesi, Burdur Merkez, Burdur

new.title: Stop for Çavdır kebabı at Kocayusuf on the Denizli road
new.desc: Çavdır kebabı is lamb or kid roasted in a clay oven, and the restaurants for it line the highway in Çavdır district. Kocayusuf, at Menevşelik on the Antalya-Denizli road, is a listed stop known for pide, buttermilk and free tea.
new.tip: A handy stop on the Antalya-Denizli road; ask for the oven kebab.
new.q: Kocayusuf, Antalya-Denizli Yolu, Menevşelik, Çavdır, Burdur

new.title: Buy Burdur ceviz ezmesi at Kayımoğlu
new.desc: Burdur walnut paste is a GI-registered sweet (2009) made from equal parts walnut, semolina and sugar, uncooked. Kayımoğlu Dondurma & Ceviz Ezmesi on Göksavaş Sokak in Konak is a central Burdur shop that also serves ice cream and baklava.
new.tip: Buy a packed box of ceviz ezmesi to take home, and add a scoop of the local dondurma while you are there.
new.q: Kayımoğlu Dondurma, Göksavaş Sokak, Konak Mahallesi, Merkez, Burdur

new.title: Visit the Sırrı Mustafa Özkan Culture House in Gölhisar
new.desc: This 1928 two-storey mansion in Gölhisar now shows regional heritage and ethnographic objects. It gives context before or after a trip to nearby Kibyra.
new.tip: Ask locally for opening times.
new.q: Muallim Mustafa Sırrı Özkan Kültür Evi, Gölhisar, Burdur
